text:
G5 is a spec gap, and the code doesn't yet do what the gap's wording says. The rule isn't in the spec, and `_pattern` counts lines of every class.

ARTIFACT gap_finding: `self-improvement.spec.md` SIL-B3 (line 156) says to require at least three runs with three distinct requests in 30 days, counting each run once and by its first recorded request, and counting machines from the shared store or the local ledger. It says nothing of the class of a counted line. A search of that spec for "class" and "designed" finds nothing on the count; the hits are SIL-B1x cause text at lines 41, 54, 89 and 96, and the SIL-AC44 prompt fields at line 219. SIL-AC47 (line 203) tests only runs, requests, the window and the exit's run. SIL-B18 (line 134), SIL-B34 (line 78), SIL-B35 (line 142), SIL-AC36 and SIL-AC37 (lines 216-217) all point to SIL-B3 for the count and add no class rule. The triage rows are at `i170c.triage.md` lines 15 (item 6: only `fault` lines count; a fixture with three `designed` lines does not file, three `fault` lines do) and 36 (G5). In code, `improve/filing.py` `_pattern` (lines 83-103) builds `same` (line 89) from history by fingerprint and window only. It does not look at `h.get("class")`, so `designed` lines count today (read). `decide` (line 144) checks only the candidate's own class, `!= "fault"` gives `record`. The classes are `fault`, `infra` and `designed`, from `causes.py:16`; `causes.py:138` and `:263` classify a decision by the starting caller as `designed`. No test of this was read.
